title: Exact conservation repairs a compressed sparse-damage resistance oracle near disconnection
reported_status: Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, quantum circuit execution, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. Recovered verify_sparse_damage.py and verification_results.json report 756 exact rational damage cases (16 infinite, 18 disconnected graph but finite selected-pair cases), 63 exact local-kernel checks, six near-cut cases down to retained 2^-200, and 9,919 randomized supports/500 damage queries. The random diagnostic uses 1,024 rows for 39 edges: it demonstrates no memory compression at scale. Dense reference diagnostics are not asymptotic or hardware benchmarks. Intake executed neither file.
scientific_scope_status: For an explicit connected undirected graph with n vertices, m edges, positive rational conductances, fixed distinct terminals s,t and sparsity k, each query chooses <=k edges with rational 0<d_e<=1, replacing w_e by (1-d_e)w_e. Every hypothetical query resets to the same undamaged reference. For epsilon in (0,1/2), failure delta, q=O(epsilon^(-2)[k log(em/k)+log(1/delta)]), the source proposes expected preprocessing O-tilde(mq), O(mq) stored working words and worst-case query arithmetic O(qk^2+k^3), with polynomial finite-bit factors. One success event covers all supports and rational severities, hence unlimited adaptive queries even inspecting the sketch. Finite terminal resistance has relative error<=epsilon; infinity is returned iff the selected terminals disconnect. An isolated component containing neither terminal does not force infinity.
